audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer gives Zac levels 2, 3, first item and 2+ items (sides Skill/Zac/Zac/Skill/Skill/Zac/Zac) while the content layer gives Gragas five straight stages. Zac wins 44.6% over 139 games — the lowest win rate in this slice.
audit.why: This is the third entry in the slice where the full-layer chart reads as though Zac is favoured in a lane he clearly loses (Galio and Garen were the others). The content chart matches the data and the content prose; the full chart contradicts both.
audit.corrected: Aligned the full layer to the content chart — Gragas through level 6, Skill at first item, Zac at 2+ items.

audit.whatIsWrong: Body Slam is named as the matchup-defining cooldown in breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.early, breakdown.mid, phases[3].why, phases[5].why and dosFull[0]. Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s.
audit.why: Body Slam barely scales — it is 14s at rank 1 and still 12s maxed, so it is never really "down" long enough to plan an all-in around. The cooldown that actually decides this lane is Explosive Cask at 100/85/70s, because it knocks Zac out of a committed Elastic Slingshot. The content layer already says this ("never E in when his ult is up without tracking it first") while the full layer points at the wrong ability.
audit.corrected: Re-pointed breakdown.cooldowns and breakdown.mid at Explosive Cask with its real number, and noted Body Slam is a stun rather than a waitable window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere mentions that Barrel Roll grows stronger the longer the cask sits before detonating.
audit.why: Riot's text: the cask "can be activated to explode or will explode on its own after 4 seconds", and "the potency of the explosion increases over time". A Zac standing next to a placed cask is taking a bigger hit every second he stays there. This is concrete positioning information and it was absent from both layers.
audit.corrected: Added the charge-up to spikes[0] and to the matching Don't.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1] is titled "Fight in his Q puddle". Barrel Roll leaves no puddle.
audit.why: Barrel Roll is a single cask that detonates once, damaging and slowing. There is no lingering ground zone, so the mental image the title gives is of the wrong ability shape — a player watching for a damage-over-time area will not be watching for the cask that is quietly gaining potency next to them.
audit.corrected: Retitled to the cask and gave the body the real reason to stay away from it.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] and early both blame Zac's Q range: "out-trade your short-range level-1 Q" and "your Q range is too short to punish".
audit.why: The range gap is 50 units — Barrel Roll is 850 and Stretching Strikes is 800. Range is not why Zac loses the level-1 trade. The real asymmetry is shape: Gragas throws an area cask that pays off without ever touching him, while Zac's Q has to actually catch a champion, and Drunken Rage then cuts what Zac deals back. Telling the player their range is the problem points them at something they cannot fix.
audit.corrected: Replaced the range explanation with the actual one in both strings.

audit.whatIsWrong: Drunken Rage is described only as damage reduction; its one-second drink is never mentioned as a tell.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Gragas samples his latest brew for 1 second." That second is a visible commitment before his empowered auto, so the drink animation — not the cask — is the cue that a trade is starting. The missing-interactions file flags this matchup for autoreset-burst-tell on Drunken Rage and nothing in the entry acted on it.
audit.corrected: Added the drink tell to breakdown.mid.

edits.before: Gragas's Barrel Roll and Drunken Rage out-trade your short-range level-1 Q.
edits.after: Barrel Roll is an area cask he lands without ever having to hit you.

edits.before: Gragas out-trades you from level 1 — Barrel Roll poke and Drunken Rage make every exchange his, and your Q range is too short to punish, so give ground and farm safely.
edits.after: Gragas out-trades you from level 1 — Barrel Roll lands as a zone at 850 while your Q has to actually catch him at 800, and Drunken Rage cuts the damage you deal back.

edits.before: Gragas dominates this window — his Barrel Roll (Q) poke plus Body Slam (E) harass out-trade your short Stretching Strikes, and his Drunken Rage (W) damage reduction lets him win any melee exchange, so farm from max range.
edits.after: Gragas dominates this window — Barrel Roll (Q) zones you and Body Slam (E) is a 14s stun, while Drunken Rage (W) cuts the damage you deal. His cask grows stronger the longer it sits, so never stand beside one waiting to pop.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 stay hard: his Q-E-W kit chunks you and Explosive Cask lets him deny your Slingshot all-ins; wait for tower or jungler and don't force it.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 stay hard: his kit chunks you and Explosive Cask, 100s at rank 1, denies your Slingshot all-ins; wait for tower or jungler and don't force it.

edits.before: - Gragas Body Slam: matchup-defining — His engage. E-knock after it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Gragas Explosive Cask: 100s at rank 1 — it knocks you straight out of a committed Slingshot, so it gates every all-in you make. - Body Slam: only 14s and it stuns, not a window you can wait out.

edits.before: Trade strictly around Body Slam: when it is down, run your full pattern; when it is up, give nothing. If ahead, freeze and starve him.
edits.after: Trade strictly around Explosive Cask: with it down run your full pattern, with it up give nothing. His 1s drink tell precedes every trade.

edits.before: Q-stretch trades and blob pickups out-sustain the early chip. Respect Gragas's Body Slam completely — the first levels are about banking small advantages, not proving a point.
edits.after: Bank blobs and XP; do not prove a point into a Gragas who cuts the damage he takes every time he drinks. His Body Slam stun on a 14s cooldown is what to respect early.

edits.before: Elastic Slingshot from fog + R bounces win every river fight. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Gragas's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Explosive Cask knocks you back out of a committed Slingshot, so from 6 onward every all-in you make happens on his terms, not yours.

edits.before: Gragas wastes Body Slam — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Blobs are your sustain and revive margin — trade along them.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: The cask hits harder the longer he lets it sit before popping it.

notes: Zac's worst matchup in the slice at 44.6%, and the full-layer chart had him favoured in four of seven stages — the third time in this slice (after Galio and Garen) that the full layer contradicts both the content layer and the win rate in a losing lane. That pattern is consistent enough to look like a generator default rather than nine independent mistakes: the full layer appears to emit a Zac-favourable chart regardless of matchup, and only the content layer tracks the data. Worth checking across the other 62 Zac entries. Substantive corrections: Body Slam was named the matchup-defining cooldown in six strings but is 14s at rank 1 and 12s maxed, so it is never down long enough to matter; Explosive Cask at 100s is what actually gates a Zac all-in, and the content layer already knew that. Also added Barrel Roll's potency ramp — the cask gets stronger the longer it sits, which is a real reason to move that was stated nowhere — and fixed "Q puddle", which describes a lingering zone Barrel Roll does not create. Finally, both whys[0] and early blamed Zac's Q range for the losing level-1 trade; the gap is 50 units (850 vs 800), so range is not the problem and a player cannot act on that diagnosis.
